newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas rises, most interest on Q3 97 and Q1 98.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas rises, most interest on Q3 97 and Q1 98.

text.p: The UK spot natural gas market saw a lot of interest in the third quarter this year and the first quarter of 1998 on Tuesday, with the volume of trade far higher than on Monday, traders and brokers said.

"People have been looking for Q3 from every angle all day long," said one seller at St Fergus who sold two tranches. "I've had a phone call every five minutes for two hours for those two deals," he added.
One company which reported involvement in six trades said it had done approximately three times that number of deals, but most were on a private and confidential basis and no details were given.
The dealer said there was a lot of nervousness in the market, leading to the confidentiality over details of trade. "Everyone's nervous of it moving," he said.

The third, fourth and first quarters all closed firmer, with Q1 posting the biggest gains. Trade was done at 16.00 pence a therm several times in that period, compared with 15.75 pence on Monday. Price rises in other periods were modest.

The only deal confirmed by both sides in Q3 at the NBP was for weekdays only at 10.40 pence a therm. One of the counterparties said that there was normally a premium of 0.30 pence a therm for weekday gas over week and weekend gas, so valuing the quarter at 10.10 pence.

But by the close, one broker saw the bid/offer spread for the quarter at 10.20/10.30 pence a therm. It was felt that some of the private and confidential deals done over the day may have been for this quarter.

The IPE futures contract was thinly traded with only 105 lots done in nine separate deals. Most months settled firmer, but there was some slippage in the afternoon, with bids even higher in the morning session than by the close - although there were only two trades totalling 20 lots done in the morning.
